**Archived at Zenodo:** [doi:10.5281/zenodo.24168326](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24168326). This DOI always resolves to the latest release of the maintained version.

```{r setup}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

here::i_am("README.qmd")

gt <- read_csv(
  here::here("ground_truth", "coppock_2025_ground_truth.csv"),
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character(), value_paper = col_character(),
                   value_script = col_double(), value_rewrite = col_double(),
                   match = col_logical(), match_rewrite = col_logical(), holds = col_logical())
)

plotted <- gt |>
  filter(str_starts(claim_id, "f1_")) |>
  mutate(panel = str_sub(claim_id, 4, 4), diff = abs(as.numeric(value_paper) - value_rewrite),
         statistic = if_else(str_ends(claim_id, "_est"), "estimate", "interval"))

fit <- function(panels, statistic_name) {
  max(plotted$diff[plotted$panel %in% panels & plotted$statistic == statistic_name])
}

descriptive <- gt |> filter(claim_type == "descriptive", !is.na(holds))
archive <- read_csv(here::here("ground_truth", "archive_run_status.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
specifications <- read_csv(here::here("maintained", "output", "figure_1b_specifications.csv"),
                           show_col_types = FALSE)
```

# Summary

This repository recomputes Figure 1 and checks the prose of a four-page review article, which reanalyzes five survey experiments from *The Power of Partisanship* (Dyck and Pearson-Merkowitz 2023). The review deposited no code and no data. Its data are the book's, from the UNC Dataverse collection, and are released under CC0.

- **Panels (a), (c), and (e) reproduce.** `r sum(plotted$panel != "b" & plotted$match_rewrite == 1)` of `r sum(plotted$panel != "b")` plotted values agree within 0.0005. The largest gaps are `r sprintf("%.4f", fit(c("a", "c", "e"), "estimate"))` on estimates and `r sprintf("%.4f", fit(c("a", "c", "e"), "interval"))` on interval ends. **The specifications behind that agreement were inferred from the plotted positions**, so it shows that this rewrite finds what was plotted. It is not an independent check that the specifications are the right ones. The panels use three different weight and party codings, which the article does not state.
- **Panel (b) reproduces from the 2014 survey, and p. 3 contradicts itself.** The review's script for the panel, `chapter_3_chamberrcontrol.R`, is in the project archive and in no deposit. This repo's rewrite follows it, and `r sum(plotted$panel == "b" & plotted$match_rewrite == 1)` of `r sum(plotted$panel == "b")` plotted values agree within 0.0005. See [Errata](#errata).
- **Panel (d) is not compared.** See [Figure verification](#figure-verification).
- **The deposit's Stata files were not run**, because Stata is not available here. `value_script` and `match` are NA throughout, so this repo has no archive-versus-page comparison.

| Link | |
|---|---|
| Article | [10.1093/psquar/qqaf037](https://doi.org/10.1093/psquar/qqaf037) |
| Data collection | UNC Dataverse, datasets listed in `original_manifest.csv`; the 2014 survey from the project archive, so a stranger cannot fetch it (`download_original.R`) |
| Errata | `coppock_2025_errata.pdf` |

To reproduce, run `Rscript run_all.R`. It fetches the 11 deposited files, verifies them against `original_manifest.csv` on MD5 and byte size, recomputes the figure, builds the ground truth, and runs the gate. The figure positions come from `ground_truth/extract_figure_1.py`, which needs the article PDF as an argument. The PDF is not redistributed here.

```
download_original.R, original_manifest.csv   the deposited surveys, not redistributed
maintained/                                  the recomputation and in_text_claims.R
ground_truth/                                the extraction, positions, ground truth, and gate
errata.qmd, coppock_2025_errata.pdf          corrections to the article
```

# Paper overview

The review argues that the book's experiments estimate the effects of party cues and of chamber control, which do not manipulate the book's main causal variable. Study 1 uses the 2018 survey, Study 2 the 2014 survey, Study 3 the 2017 survey, Study 4 the 2020 survey, and Study 5 the 2019 survey.

The 2018 survey holds free-text responses in `Q149`, one of which includes a respondent's email address. Nothing in this repo reads or redistributes that column, and the file comes from the public deposit rather than from this repo.

# Original archive reproducibility

The review itself has nothing to run. The book's Stata files are in `original/` once fetched and were not executed. All 11 files match the manifest. `ground_truth/run_archive.R` records each of the `r n_distinct(archive$script)` Stata files as `not_run` in both passes in `ground_truth/archive_run_status.csv`, and `ground_truth/archive_overwrites.csv` has no rows. The maintained code is a rewrite in R from the deposited `.dta` files, not a port of the `.do` files.

# Errata

`coppock_2025_errata.pdf` carries two entries, defined in `errata.qmd` and written to `errata_entries.csv`.

1. **Study 2, corrected.** The first two Study 2 sentences contradicted the third and Figure 1(b), which agree with each other and with the 2014 survey (Republicans `r sprintf("%.3f", specifications$estimate[specifications$party == "Republican" & specifications$survey == 2014 & specifications$weighted])`, Democrats `r sprintf("%.3f", specifications$estimate[specifications$party == "Democrat" & specifications$survey == 2014 & specifications$weighted])`). The entry corrects them to "less conservative" and "more liberal" (review queue row 64, 2026-11-07). The repeat in the 2018 survey has the opposite signs, and the review does not plot it. All these intervals cover zero.
2. **A dropped verb in Study 3.** "whether they given no cue" should read "whether they are given no cue".

# The extraction and the two instruments

`ground_truth/published_claims.csv` holds `r nrow(gt)` rows: `r sum(gt$claim_type == "pipeline")` plotted values, `r sum(gt$claim_type == "descriptive")` descriptive claims, and `r sum(gt$claim_type %in% c("structural", "definitional", "transcribed"))` structural, definitional, or transcribed tokens. The article prints no estimate as a number. Its figure is vector, so `extract_figure_1.py` converts each mark through its panel's axis ticks. The positions take nothing from the data.

`ground_truth/build_ground_truth.R` joins those positions to the recomputation, and computes each descriptive claim across cells. `maintained/in_text_claims.R` selects the same quantities cell by cell. `ground_truth/claims_gate.R` runs the second as a program, requires one printed line per declared claim in both directions, requires the two instruments to agree at the printed precision, and requires every claim id in the errata spine to name an extraction row.

Both instruments read the same output files, so their agreement is evidence about the selection and arithmetic. It says nothing about whether the inferred specification is the one the review used.

# Coverage

```{r}
gt |>
  count(claim_type, verdict = case_when(
    !is.na(match_rewrite) & match_rewrite == 1 ~ "matches",
    !is.na(match_rewrite) & match_rewrite == 0 ~ "does not match",
    !is.na(holds) & holds == 1 ~ "holds",
    !is.na(holds) & holds == 0 ~ "does not hold",
    .default = "no verdict"
  )) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Claim type", "Verdict", "Rows"))
```

**The nine descriptive verdicts are about direction.** Study 2's first two sentences hold in sign while every interval covers zero. In Study 1, all four two-thirds signs hold, while the interval for Republicans under the Republican cue covers zero, which sits uneasily with "clear evidence".

**Some claims have no verdict.** The abstract's summary states no scope, so the share of panel (a) and (e) cells with its signs (`r sprintf("%.2f", gt$value_rewrite[gt$claim_id == "abstract_cue_pattern"])`) carries no verdict. The sentence saying the reanalyses arrive at the authors' estimates is not tested, because this repo holds no copy of the book's printed estimates. The book's page and year are unchecked for the same reason. Footnote 3's citation was checked against Crossref on 2026-11-05.

# Number-by-number comparison

```{r}
plotted |>
  group_by(panel) |>
  summarise(values = n(), within_tolerance = sum(match_rewrite == 1),
            max_gap_estimate = sprintf("%.4f", max(diff[statistic == "estimate"])),
            max_gap_interval = sprintf("%.4f", max(diff[statistic == "interval"]))) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Panel", "Values", "Within 0.0005", "Largest estimate gap", "Largest interval gap"))
```

The tolerance is set once in `build_ground_truth.R` and is half of the third decimal. It is wider than the largest gap in the panels that reproduce, and no precision of the marks was measured independently. Panel (b)'s row compares with the weighted difference in means on the 2014 survey, as the review's script computes it. `maintained/output/figure_1b_specifications.csv` also reports the unweighted one and both on the 2018 repeat.

# Maintained rewrite

`maintained/figure_1_panels.R` computes each panel with `lm_robust` as a difference in means between cue and no cue within party. The specifications are as follows.

| Panel | Study | Survey | Weights | Party |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| a | 1 | 2018 | none | pid7, 1 to 3 and 5 to 7 |
| b | 2 | 2014 | survey | pid7, 1 to 3 and 5 to 7 |
| c | 3 | 2017 | none | pid7, 1 to 3 and 5 to 7 |
| d | 4 | 2020 | none | pid7, slopes and cue means only |
| e | 5 | 2019 | survey | pid3, 1 and 2 |

The script asserts the survey's 40 percent labels and the direction of the candidate scale at the point of use.

# Figure verification {#figure-verification}

The figure is not redrawn. Its check is the comparison above, which uses the positions of the published marks.

**Panel (d) is not read from the PDF.** The marks are points, lines, and ribbons across cue, cost, and party, so reading them would mean inferring a further specification for a comparison the review's sentences do not need. Those two sentences state direction only, and the recomputed cost slopes and cue means test them. A plotting error in panel (d) would not be caught here.
